correctness.rationale: For each index j the original Bernstein node j/n lies in the separate interval [j/(n+1),(j+1)/(n+1)]. Constructing one continuous piecewise-linear function with slope +1 up to this node and -1 afterwards makes the signed Lipschitz bound equal the sum of all cell displacements, so the exact norm is (n+1)^(-1) E|J/n-U| even for arbitrary cell mixing laws. The centered mean condition E U=x and Jensen give minimizer U=x; equality for all positive binomial weights forces U supported on the two grid neighbors of x, degenerating to a point at integral nx and endpoints. The continuous Dirac selection attains the global infimum. De Moivre binomial MAD on cell k has value 2*C(n-1,k)*x^(k+1)*(1-x)^(n-k), unique within-cell peak (k+1)/(n+1); discrete strict log-concavity of h(s)=s^(s+1)/s! yields the unique odd-degree and double even-degree maxima. Stirling gives D_n/(n+1)~1/(sqrt(2*pi)*n^(3/2)). Independent rational W1 integration over 195 (n,x,nu) configurations and the all-cell exact parity maximization in n=1..13 agree. This finite evidence does not prove the infinite claims.
residual_risks: The De Moivre identity is classical, and the prior successive-degree Bernstein result supplies a special Bernoulli-jitter case, not the constrained minimax.

originality.rationale: The novel assertion is the attained constrained minimax over x-dependent centered laws, its universal signed Lipschitz extremizer and all equality distributions, not the classical binomial MAD or the previously proved Bernoulli mixing case. The 2016 generalized Kantorovich operator treats a fixed auxiliary measure for each degree and gives rates/preservation; the 2024 affine-preserving construction averages about each j/n and studies shape preserving, not this optimal cell-insertion law. The known exact B_(n+1)-B_n norm corresponds to U~Bernoulli(x), which is generally not optimal.
